caveats: Results are per determination. The row count is not the sample size: one determination covers most of the rows.

There is no positive control. Every scorable row sits on a methodology ICVCM rejected, so a model answering 'weak' to everything would score full marks on the strength arm, and §3.2 has nothing to measure at all.
The corpus is Carbonmark's REST catalogue, not the deployed x402 inventory, whose methodology strings join to no ICVCM decision.
methodologyStrength and adverseFindings are disclosure and do not gate a retirement. Only integrityFlags do.
namesAuthority and namesConcern are keyword matches over the findings text, which is published in full alongside so the judgement can be checked.

adverseFindings: Large hydroelectric dam projects, including grid-connected hydro under ACM0002, have been widely and repeatedly challenged in the carbon market literature on additionality grounds — many such projects were found likely to have been built regardless of carbon finance given favorable economics and government support for hydropower in Türkiye during this period.

The credits are from 2012-2014 vintages (10-14 years old), which predates significant tightening of additionality and financial-barrier testing standards for hydro projects under VCS; older vintages of this type have faced particular scrutiny for being 'zombie credits' from projects that would have proceeded without carbon revenue.

ACM0002 is a large, generic methodology applied across thousands of renewable projects globally, and hydro applications specifically have been flagged in third-party analyses (e.g. academic and NGO studies of CDM/VCS hydro credits) as having some of the weakest additionality evidence among renewable energy credit types.

Dams and hydroelectric facilities can carry contested co-benefit and environmental-impact profiles (e.g. river ecology, displacement, downstream effects) that are separate from the carbon accounting itself but relevant to overall project quality perception.
